contexts.api_surface: Outbound: POST to configured webhook URL / ntfy endpoint
contexts.description: Delivers breach, warning, error-spike, and relay-dead-letter notifications over webhook (generic HTTP POST) and ntfy channels. Includes rejection-count attribution so alerts identify which models/operations are consuming the most quota. Dedup and per-channel cooldowns prevent alert storms.
contexts.name: alert-delivery

contexts.api_surface: POST /webhook, GET /health (served); calls GET /v1/events, GET /v1/scores (outbound to LightTrack API), Resend email API
contexts.description: The lt-responder binary — an autonomous daemon that receives LightTrack alert webhooks, classifies them as transient vs. code-side, fetches failing events for context, runs Claude Code in read-only mode to diagnose the root cause, optionally attempts a gated auto-fix, writes a Markdown report, and emails it via Resend. A circuit breaker caps concurrent investigations and per-project frequency to prevent runaway costs.
contexts.name: alert-responder

contexts.description: The lt-api binary entry point: wires together store selection (SQLite/Postgres/Firestore from DSN), price book seeding, router construction, and Axum server startup. Also provides AppState, the redaction policy cache warmed on the blocking startup thread, and all auth middleware (Bearer key extraction, dev vs. enforced mode, admin vs. project-key principal resolution).
contexts.name: api-server

contexts.api_surface: POST /v1/projects/:id/benchmarks, GET /v1/projects/:id/benchmarks, GET /v1/benchmarks/:id, GET /v1/benchmarks/:id/runs, GET /v1/benchmarks/:id/gate, POST /v1/benchmark-runs, POST /v1/benchmarks/:id/enqueue, GET/POST/PUT /v1/jobs
contexts.description: Defines, runs, and gates benchmark evaluations against versioned datasets. Supports simple-score, multi-dimension rubric, and compare/pairwise modes. The CI gate endpoint maps benchmark verdict against a baseline to a pass/regressed/no_baseline/no_runs result with a corresponding exit code for CI pipelines. Jobs serve as the async dispatch mechanism for benchmark runs.
contexts.name: benchmark-management

contexts.description: Normalises revenue from Stripe and Polar billing providers into canonical RevenueEvent records. Verifies cryptographically signed webhooks (HMAC-SHA256 for Stripe, Standard Webhooks for Polar), converts foreign-currency amounts to USD using a static FX rate book with ISO-4217 minor-unit awareness, and collapses duplicate refund deliveries via idempotency keys.
contexts.name: billing-integration

contexts.description: The lt operator CLI — a thin HTTP client over the API for everyday administrative tasks: project/key management, usage limit CRUD (with dimension scoping and soft-warning thresholds), cost queries, event and trace browsing, profit margin inspection, and collective leaderboard participation including the two-hop contribute flow. Renders Markdown tables on TTY; raw JSON when piped.
contexts.name: cli-tool

contexts.api_surface: Calls: POST /v1/events on the LightTrack API
contexts.description: Fire-and-forget ingest SDKs for monitored applications written in Python and Rust. Both use a background worker thread/channel so tracking never blocks the application. Provide OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini field-mapping helpers, a span context manager for trace propagation, and SDK-level auto-patching for zero-code instrumentation. Best-effort design — never throws into the application.
contexts.name: client-sdks

contexts.description: The pure, I/O-free shared domain model for the entire workspace. Every other crate imports types from here; this crate has no dependencies on network, disk, or other workspace crates. Contains the canonical data structures, the shared LtError type, and the new_id() UUIDv4 generator.
contexts.name: core-types

contexts.description: Maintains a DB-backed model price book seeded from config/pricing.json and supports live hot-swap via PUT. Cost attribution runs at ingest time using provider+model lookup with prompt-length tier, batch, and flex-pricing variant support. Exposes cost summary and per-prompt/use-case breakdown endpoints.
contexts.name: cost-pricing

contexts.api_surface: POST /v1/projects/:id/datasets, GET /v1/projects/:id/datasets, GET /v1/datasets/:id, POST /v1/datasets/:id/items, GET /v1/datasets/:id/items, POST /v1/datasets/:id/freeze
contexts.description: Manages versioned evaluation datasets of input/output/expected triples sourced from real events or manual curation. Supports item-level append, freeze (making a dataset immutable for reproducible benchmarks), and an automated sampling pipeline in lt-runner that strips PII from live events before freezing.
contexts.name: dataset-management

contexts.api_surface: Calls: POST /v1/relay/lease, POST /v1/relay/tasks/:id/result on configured cloud sources
contexts.description: The lt-agent binary that runs on-device and executes cloud-dispatched tasks. It long-polls for leased RelayTasks, loads the matching action from a local library (prompt template + model config + optional JSON schema), invokes Claude Code, and delivers the structured result back to the cloud via the relay API or a connector (HTTP POST or subprocess pipe). Path-traversal validation prevents action-library escapes.
contexts.name: device-agent

contexts.description: Captures every LLM call event flowing into a monitored application. Single and batch ingest endpoints validate timestamps and body sizes, attribute costs from the price book, enforce usage limits, apply PII redaction, and persist to the store with per-item accepted/rejected/invalid outcomes. Depends on limit-enforcement for admission control and pii-scrubbing for payload sanitisation.
contexts.name: event-ingest

contexts.description: Measures the reliability of the LLM judge by comparing its scores against human labels using Cohen's κ, Pearson correlation, MAE, and RMSE. A drift sentinel mode runs periodically and raises alerts when κ degrades below the trust threshold. Calibration data lives in a JSONL golden set.
contexts.name: judge-calibration

contexts.api_surface: Calls: Anthropic claude -p subprocess, POST generativelanguage.googleapis.com (Gemini), POST api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions
contexts.description: Core LLM-as-judge execution engine that drives Anthropic Claude (via subprocess), Google Gemini, and OpenAI REST APIs to generate candidate outputs and produce structured evaluation verdicts. Implements retry/backoff on 429/5xx, JSON extraction with one-shot repair, deterministic sampling, pairwise A-vs-B comparison, and multi-sample rubric judging with k-sample averaging and agreement metrics.
contexts.name: judge-engine

contexts.description: Per-project usage caps that can throttle or block ingest traffic when cost, call-count, or token thresholds are exceeded within configurable rolling windows (hour/day/month). Rules support fine-grained scoping by provider, model, or operation name. An in-memory usage cache makes admission O(1) and TOCTOU-safe. Rejected ingest attempts are tracked in-memory for attribution reporting.
contexts.name: limit-enforcement

contexts.api_surface: POST /v1/revenue, GET /v1/margin, GET /v1/margin/trend, GET /v1/margin/customer/:id, GET /v1/margin/simulate, POST /v1/billing/:provider/webhook
contexts.description: Ingests revenue events from billing providers and computes profit margin (revenue minus LLM cost) sliced by project, customer, product, model, or use-case. Exposes trend series, per-customer breakdowns, and a pricing what-if simulator that projects margin under hypothetical token price changes. Revenue events are stored with period_start/period_end for subscription proration.
contexts.name: margin-analytics

contexts.api_surface: MCP stdio JSON-RPC 2.0; calls all GET + selected POST/PUT/DELETE endpoints of the LightTrack API
contexts.description: The lt-mcp binary — a Model Context Protocol server exposing LightTrack observability data to Claude Code and other MCP-aware agents over stdio JSON-RPC 2.0. Provides 25 read-only tools and 11 write tools (gated behind LIGHTTRACK_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES). It is a thin HTTP client of the API; it never touches the database and cannot crash the API process. Write tools on the MCP surface intentionally exclude secret-minting operations.
contexts.name: mcp-server

contexts.description: Opt-in privacy-safe model performance network where participating LightTrack instances contribute k-anonymised benchmark digests to a shared hub. Digests aggregate quality, cost, and latency per model-task-judge triple without exposing raw prompt data. Merged leaderboard enables cross-organisation model comparison with rubric-fingerprint alignment.
contexts.name: model-leaderboard

contexts.description: Regex-based PII scrubber that is the fast structured-PII phase of the anonymisation pipeline. Redacts emails, IBANs, US SSNs, API secrets (sk-… / AKIA…), hex secrets, credit cards, IPs, and phone numbers with typed placeholders in a single deterministic pass. Applied at ingest time for payload redaction and in the dataset builder before freezing.
contexts.name: pii-scrubbing

contexts.description: Projects future spend and margin using EWMA and linear trend models over daily counter series. Emits pre-emptive budget-breach and margin-erosion alerts before limits are actually hit. Configurable horizon and lookback window; daily usage bucketing requires no extra schema columns.
contexts.name: predictive-forecast

contexts.description: Multi-tenant project and API key lifecycle management. Projects are the top-level tenancy boundary; each has a redaction policy (none/hash/drop) and a collective opt-in flag. API keys are prefix-hashed bearer tokens with revocation support and last-used tracking.
contexts.name: project-management

contexts.api_surface: POST /v1/projects/:id/prompts, GET /v1/projects/:id/prompts, GET /v1/projects/:id/prompts/:name, POST /v1/projects/:id/prompts/:name/versions, GET /v1/projects/:id/prompts/:name/versions, POST /v1/projects/:id/prompts/:name/promote
contexts.description: Stores and versions prompts by name with label-based aliasing (e.g. 'production', 'canary'). Promoting a label to a new version auto-enqueues a benchmark run and is blocked if the run regresses against the baseline — making the registry a quality-gated deployment mechanism for prompts.
contexts.name: prompt-registry

contexts.description: Cloud-to-device task queue enabling on-device Claude Code runs triggered from a cloud dashboard without requiring inbound connections to the device. Tasks move through queued→leased→succeeded/dead lifecycle with retry logic, idempotency keys, and lease deadlines. A flat-cost revenue event is recorded on successful settlement.
contexts.name: relay-queue

contexts.description: Markdown rendering for analytics and evaluation entities: benchmarks, datasets, rubrics, comparison leaderboards, forecast reports, collective digests, prompt listings, and margin analytics. Shares the common table helpers from rendering-core. Populated by both the CLI and MCP server.
contexts.name: rendering-analytics

contexts.description: Converts LightTrack API JSON responses for operational entities into aligned Markdown tables for use by the lt CLI and lt-mcp MCP server. Covers events, traces, scores, prices, projects, jobs, limits, costs, and the shared Markdown table helpers. Pure serde_json::Value in, Markdown string out — no database or core crate dependency.
contexts.name: rendering-core

contexts.description: Defines and stores structured evaluation rubrics composed of weighted, anchor-point dimensions (RCAF methodology). Rubrics are referenced by benchmarks and used by the judge engine to produce per-dimension scores with an overall pass/fail threshold. The runner invokes rubric judging with k-sample averaging for reliability.
contexts.name: rubric-system

contexts.api_surface: Calls all /v1/* endpoints of the LightTrack API
contexts.description: The lt-runner binary — the local scoring and benchmark worker that runs alongside the developer's Claude CLI and API keys. Handles the worker-queue serve loop (claim job → run benchmark → finish), periodic dataset-sampling scheduler, recurring benchmark sweeps, and the Stripe billing sync command. It talks to the API exclusively over HTTP and never touches the database directly.
contexts.name: runner-worker

contexts.description: Records and retrieves LLM-as-judge scores for individual events and whole traces. The online scoring loop in lt-runner polls for unscored events, judges them via the engine, and POSTs scores back. Scores carry dimension breakdown, pass/fail verdict, reasoning text, and attribution cost.
contexts.name: scoring

contexts.api_surface: Calls: Firestore REST API at firestore.googleapis.com
contexts.description: Firestore backend implementing the Store trait over the Firestore REST API using blocking reqwest (no gRPC), supporting both the Firestore emulator for local/CI and production GCP via OAuth bearer token. Schemaless — collections are created on first write. Adds the prompt registry implementation not yet in the Postgres backend, and handles aggregation client-side due to Firestore query limitations.
contexts.name: store-firestore

contexts.description: Defines the backend-agnostic Store trait (~50 methods) covering every domain entity and the shared StoreError type. Includes codec helpers for timestamp/enum/JSON encoding that all backends share, and a conformance test suite that any backend implementation must pass. The admission logic (evaluate_admission) and EventFilter/EventPage keyset-pagination types live here.
contexts.name: store-interface

contexts.description: Postgres backend implementing the full Store trait via sqlx, targeting managed services (Neon, Cloud SQL, RDS, Supabase). Wraps an async PgPool with a Tokio runtime so the synchronous Store interface can block_on queries from spawn_blocking callers in the API. Uses FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED RETURNING for concurrency-safe job and relay-task dequeuing.
contexts.name: store-postgres

contexts.description: SQLite implementation of the Store trait for the core operational entities: events (with index-seekable project+timestamp queries), projects and API keys, limit rules and usage cache (O(1) rolling admission), and model prices. The UsageCache is a mutex-guarded in-memory structure locked before the connection to ensure TOCTOU-safe admission.
contexts.name: store-sqlite-core

contexts.description: SQLite backend modules for evaluation, scheduling, and extended-domain entities: benchmarks and runs, datasets and items, rubrics, async jobs, versioned prompts, relay tasks, revenue events, daily forecast counters, and collective leaderboard entries. Integration and timestamp-format conformance tests also live here.
contexts.name: store-sqlite-eval

contexts.description: Groups LLM events by trace_id into derived rollup records with a span tree and per-trace cost/latency totals. Supports keyset-paginated trace listing and a dedicated whole-trace scoring endpoint. No new schema tables — traces are a query-time aggregation of the events table.
contexts.name: trace-analytics
